newsitem.title: UK: LUKoil said eyeing Ventspils Nafta stake.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil said eyeing Ventspils Nafta stake.

text.p: Russia's LUKoil has expressed interest in taking a 30 percent stake in Latvia's Ventspils Nafta oil terminal but it will not be allowed a controlling share, a senior Latvian official said on Monday.

"LUKoil expressed the wish to buy 30 percent of the shares," Janis Naglis, head of the Baltic state's privatisation agency, told Reuters at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

But Naglis said such a large stake in the soon-to-be- privatised terminal, the main Baltic export outlet for Russian crude oil and refined oil products, would not be concentrated in the hands of any single investor.

"Please come and buy shares but there will be no special quantity for anyone," he said. "Everybody is obliged to compete on an equal basis. If they (LUKoil) are prepared to pay money they can come and buy shares."

Naglis said the privatisation should raise about 150 million lats ($300 million) for Latvia, with the first stage of the privatisation taking place by July 1. This stage will involve selling off the state stake in the LaSam pipeline company and merging it with Ventspils Nafta.
Crude oil and refined products arrive at Ventspils via pipeline from Samara in Russia and via railway.
LUKoil is one of the main clients of the port, which handled about 25 million tonnes of crude and products last year and made unaudited profits of 34 million lats.
Naglis said a total of 210 million shares, each with a face value of one lat, would be sold by the end of this year.
"No less than 26 percent will remain in state hands in the first stage of privatisation," he added.

About 15 percent would be distributed in a public offering and about 15 percent through an issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs), while 0.75 percent would be sold to employees through privatisation vouchers, he said.
The privatisation also envisages tendering seven percent of shares to foreign investors. Naglis said the revenues could be used to rebuild the pipeline system, he said.
This may involve an agreement with Russia, Belarus and Lithuania, whose territory the pipeline crosses.
